date_note: Police issued their statement late on Thursday 26 November, per AFP via Arab News (published 27 November).
title: Indian police rescue 164 foreign nationals allegedly trafficked and forced into cyber fraud near New Delhi
geo_basis: suburb of New Delhi as stated by the article; coordinates are of New Delhi
summary: AFP reports that Indian police said they had rescued 164 foreign nationals, including 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, in a crackdown on an international cybercrime network in a suburb of New Delhi. Police said that after arrival the foreign nationals were allegedly confined and compelled to take part in cyber fraud. A Malaysian national was arrested and two Indian handlers identified.
plain: Indian police say they rescued 164 foreigners who were lured with job offers and then allegedly forced into online fraud. A Malaysian was arrested and two Indian handlers identified.
exec: Police in India say they rescued 164 foreign nationals allegedly forced into online fraud, a sign that scam-compound operations also run there.

evidence.quote: Indian police said they had rescued 164 foreign nationals
The victims included 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians

validation.note: Only the AFP report (Arab News) was read; the Manila Times and Arab News Pakistan copies are the same wire report. The police statement is quoted by AFP; the police page was not read.
